title: Pan latch strands when the settings modal (or placement) opens mid-drag; stale pan_last jumps the camera afterward
detail: Releases clear the latch only inside the pan branch. When panel_open or placing diverts the chain, releases (real or synthesized) are swallowed with panning set; the poll guard then re-fires a synthetic release every frame, and a stale pan_last pans on close.
recommended_fix: Clear panning/pan_last whenever a left release is swallowed (panel, placement) or dropped unhandled in dispatch_frame; re-anchor pan_last before the latch can re-engage.

title: effect_pan scales drag deltas by the eased zoom TARGET, not the live scale its comments promise
detail: Comments promise live-scale conversion; the call passes cam_zoom_to. While a wheel ease converges, content renders at cam_zoom, so pan deltas mis-track the cursor by the target/live ratio.
recommended_fix: Pass app.cam_zoom (live) as the scale to camera_pan_center, matching effect_zoom's live-transform anchoring; reconcile the comments.

title: v2 loader applies the pullback byte before rejecting other out-of-range fields — the 'defaults' fallback is not DEFAULT_A11Y
detail: A valid pullback byte is applied before the shared range checks; a file with pullback=0 plus an invalid palette/motion/scale byte returns defaults-except-pullback — not DEFAULT_A11Y. Existing out-of-range tests all use byte 1, masking it.
recommended_fix: Apply payload bytes only after every range check passes, or reset s to DEFAULT_A11Y() on each rejection; add a mixed-corruption test with pullback=0.

detail: No accumulation state is added anywhere in the diff; i32(delta) truncates sub-notch deltas to zero every frame, so slow trackpad scrolling never zooms despite the claimed behavior.
recommended_fix: Accumulate fractional GetMouseWheelMove values in Input and emit whole-notch Mouse_Wheel events when the accumulator crosses ±1, or correct the PR claim.

title: camera_spawn_is_seed 'exact mirror' breaks for multi-spawn frames: same-burst siblings join the distance set
detail: Only the candidate id is excluded; same-frame burst siblings (spawned after the candidate's core evaluation) join the terminal set, flipping seeds to attach so the pullback can miss genuine new districts.
recommended_fix: Exclude all same-slice spawned ids from the sibling set when classifying, or classify each spawn against only terminals older than it.

title: 'ONE source' comment is false: the fit derivation is duplicated inline in camera_update
detail: camera_update still derives fit inline (the context line), so the identical min() now lives in both camera_fit and camera_update — the 'ONE source' claim is false and drift-prone.
recommended_fix: Make camera_update use camera_fit(v) (or a shared render-side helper) so the derivation truly has one source.

title: PR claims 4 camera-math tests; camera_test.odin adds 6
evidence:
- New pins: 4 camera-math tests (app/render/camera_test.odin) + 4 input
  wiring tests (app/input/camera_input_test.odin) + 4 pullback tests
detail: camera_test.odin defines six @(test) procs — spawn_is_seed, pullback_target, zoom_step, anchor_center, pan_center, clamp_center — the PR's '4 camera-math tests' undercounts them.
recommended_fix: Correct the PR body count to six.

title: 'panned release never click-selects' assertion cannot fail — nothing was selected beforehand
evidence:
dispatch_frame(&ictx, []Device_Event{Device_Event(Mouse_Release{pos = {750, 550}, button = .Left})})
testing.expect(t, !ictx.panning, "the release closes the pan latch")
testing.expect(t, len(log) == 0, "the pan produced no commands")
testing.expect(t, ictx.sel_pipe == -1 && ictx.sel_node == -1, "a panned release never click-selects (the moved-check suppresses the Select)")
detail: The fixture selects nothing and the release is on empty ground; sel stays -1 whether or not the Select intent fires, so the moved-check suppression this test claims to pin is untested.
recommended_fix: Select a node before the pan, then assert sel_node is unchanged after the release; or observe the Select through a hook or command log.

title: camera_clamp_center test comment ('x is free', '960px viewport') contradicts its own both-axes-pin assertion
detail: At z=1 the 1280px window spans 1280/FIT42 ≈ 1386 world px, exceeding the 1040-wide world — both axes pin, as the assertion expects; the comment's 'x is free / 960px viewport' reasoning is wrong.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the comment: at the fit the viewport exceeds the world on both axes, so both coordinates clamp to the world center.
